clues.title: Pole: Curvy poles
text: Many wooden utility poles, particularly in the eastern parts of Bolivia are noticeably curvy and appear to be made from locally sourced tree trunks.

clues.title: Landscape: Death road
text: Northeast of La Paz, there is an unpaved road that is cloudy and wet and narrow and looks like a nightmare to drive. Yet, apparently, it is frequented by mountain bikers a whole lot.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Concrete Roads
text: Bolivia has a lot of standard asphalt roads, but concrete slab roads are also fairly common.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Curvy Poles
text: Many wooden utility poles, particularly in the eastern parts of Bolivia’s Street View coverage, are noticeably curvy and look like they are made from locally sourced tree trunks.
While you may see slightly bent poles in other places, extremely curvy poles are a very good clue for Bolivia.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Cobblestone Roads
text: There are also a lot of cobblestone roads.
These roads often have a specific pattern, with several neat lines of stones separating the more disorganised cobblestones in between.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: White Car
text: Bolivia only has Generation 3 camera coverage.
All of the country was covered by a white Google car with no antenna.
In Latin America, white cars with no antenna can also be found in Peru and Chile.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Red Rocks
text: If you have a tough 50-50, it can help to look at the colour of the rocks and soil, which often have a distinct reddish tint in Bolivia, more so than the other Andean countries.
This information should be used with a fair amount of caution, as there are many variables.
Only use it when you have no other clues available.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Architecture
text: Many buildings in Bolivia consist of large red bricks.
Buildings often have an ‘unfinished' look.
This style of architecture is also common in parts of Peru.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Northern Altiplano
text: The grasslands of the Altiplano tend to look more lush in the more northern half: the area close to El Alto and La Paz.
NOTE: Due to seasonal coverage, there are some exceptions to this, but in general this is a good rule of thumb to distinguish between the different parts of the Altiplano.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Southern Altiplano
text: The Altiplano looks more arid in the more southern half: around Oruro, and the roads going southwest towards Chile.
NOTE: There is one major exception to this: one driving side of the divided part of Ruta 1 looks somewhat green all the way up to Oruro (due to this coverage being captured in a different season).

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Lake Titicaca
text: Lake Titicaca, on the border with Peru, is the most significant body of water in Bolivia. It is located entirely within the Altiplano. The landscape around Titicaca is very green, compared to most of the western half of Bolivia.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Santa Cruz Area
text: Within the tropical area of Bolivia, coverage on unpaved roads is only found around Santa Cruz. These roads again prominently have the pink soil that is very characteristic of the area east of Andes.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Wider Santa Cruz Area
text: The area east of the Andes is very green and tropical, with lots of agriculture – especially around Santa Cruz. This area is mostly very flat, though you will see large hills on some of the roads closer to the Andes. The soil tends to have a pink colour.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Chile Border Desert
text: Between the villages of Villa Catalina and Coipasa, there is an isolated stretch of coverage where the Google car drove through extremely arid desert terrain. This small road is located close to the southwestern end of Ruta 12, near the Chilean border. It can be hard to spot on the map, because it blends in with the salt flat. Closer to Villa Catalina, the car drove over the salt flat. Closer to Coipasa, the car drove on an unpaved dirt road, where you can see cone-shaped volcanic hills. In both parts, there is virtually no vegetation.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Sajama National Park
text: Sajama National Park was covered by this unique Google car: it has a black roof rack with a series of metal bars. The coverage is on an unpaved road surrounded by fluffy bushes. The Nevado Sajama volcano is always visible. The car briefly drove through the small village of Tomarapi, which can be recognized by its traditional buildings with adobe walls and thatched roofs.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Guardrail: Unique Guardrail
text: Guardrails sometimes feature yellow and black markings. These markings always have the yellow stripes on the outside.
NOTE: Peru has similar markings. However, in Peru, the markings have the inverse colour scheme: the black stripes are always on the outside.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: Bolivia
text: Bolivia has short, white licence plates with blue text. The blue text can be hard to see through the blur, so plates might appear as plain white.
Most useful for distinguishing Bolivia from Peru which has either white or yellow license plates.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
